requirement_paraphrase: UL 4600 Ed. 3 (2023): safety argument for vehicles operating autonomously without expected human intervention; scope includes foreseeable misuse and physical attacks, and detailed information security is largely out of scope (catalogue summary; clause numbers not seen).
applies_to: Autonomous vehicles/products (UL 4600 is not itself law; may be required by contract or referenced by a regulator)

requirement_paraphrase: UL 4600 Ed. 3 (2023) describes its requirements as necessary but possibly not sufficient for a well formed safety case, with non exhaustive prompt lists (catalogue summary; clause 1.6 not seen).

instrument: UNECE WP.29 ADS regulation (reported as GTR No. 26 / UN Regulation No. 185; doc ECE-TRANS-WP.29-2026-139e)
requirement_paraphrase: Reported UNECE framework (adopted 24 June 2026) with GTR No. 26 and companion UN Regulation 185 requires a documented safety case showing no unreasonable risk and an audited lifecycle safety management system, with compliance shown by simulation, closed-track and real-world validation; entry into force and national adoption are still pending.
applies_to: L3-L5 ADS vehicles in jurisdictions applying the UN instrument

requirement_paraphrase: Reported to require a data storage system, reporting of critical events with follow-up reports within 30 days where required, and annual safety data; the specific event categories were not seen in the source.
Reported to assume ADS software does not change driving behaviour through in-vehicle learning, and to require cybersecurity controls, software update processes and remote termination capability.

instrument: Dubai Law No. (4) of 2020 regulating drone activity in Dubai
edition_or_version: Issued 2020; effective on Official Gazette publication per Media Office

applies_to: Drone operators, manufacturers, owners in Dubai

requirement_paraphrase: UAS components essential to safe operation must meet an airworthiness design standard. From SAIL IV EASA verification via a design verification report is expected; at SAIL V-VI a (restricted) type certificate under Part 21. EASA Special Condition Light-UAS is the recommended standard. Experimental flights may be accepted without recognised standards.
